gen-gf-over-the-rainbow-fs-public-sans: Public Sans comes in hefty and trustworthy, with broad open curves. Under Over the Rainbow's wobbly pen-drawn headings, a longer page would read steadily, the loose handwriting giving way to solid, easygoing lines.
gen-gf-over-the-rainbow-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp and thick, a dense strip of text with letters held open. Over the Rainbow does the loose, personal handwriting, the thin rod-bent strokes of a casual hand; Supreme does the sturdy, plain sans work of carrying the words.
gen-gf-over-the-rainbow-general-sans: General Sans reads smooth and tidy, its tall x-height filling the line with steady strokes. Its strongest quality is the way it grounds Over the Rainbow's thin, wandering handwriting without flattening any of its casual charm.
gen-gf-over-the-rainbow-manrope: Approachable from the first glance, Manrope leaves a bright gap at every curve, with hardly any step up to its capitals. Shrink Over the Rainbow too far, though, and its thin rod-like lines fade.
gen-gf-over-the-rainbow-satoshi: Casual meets crisp here: a scribbled, pen-and-paper heading above a tall, friendly sans. And Satoshi keeps its wide-open e relaxed across a long page, every stroke cut to one width, so the reading never feels cramped.
gen-gf-over-the-rainbow-switzer: Thin steel rod, bent into loose letters with a shallow curl at the ends: that's Over the Rainbow. Switzer answers with tubular, wire-like forms and a tall waist line, so the handwriting and the sans-serif text feel like cousins.
gen-gf-pangolin-fs-asap: Pangolin looks drawn with a single nib, its tall lowercase friendly and relaxed. Asap follows in a readable sans whose open-arc c and near-capital body height would carry a longer passage without effort.
gen-gf-pangolin-fs-epilogue: Loose nib-drawn friendliness on top, wiry curves below. Epilogue's tall-bodied lowercase and stubby ascenders look best when the body text stays a notch smaller than Pangolin's generous headings.
gen-gf-pangolin-fs-erode: Erode reads dignified and editorial, with a tall middle band and gently shifting stroke weight. Pangolin's rod-made handwriting sits above it, and a longer passage in the classic serif feels steady, a little formal after the casual heading.
gen-gf-pangolin-fs-fira-sans: Pangolin's single-nib look, with tall, generous lowercase, gives the heading its relaxed charm. And Fira Sans, with its large x-height and wide-open s curves, feels clean and sensible beside that handwriting.
